items.title: Gujarat High Court rejects Asaram's plea for 20-day temporary bail to meet ailing wife
items.summary: The Gujarat High Court on Wednesday rejected a plea by self-styled godman Asaram seeking 20 days' temporary bail to meet his wife, who is undergoing treatment at a hospital in Ahmedabad [Ashumal @ Asharam v State of Gujarat] . A Division Bench of Justices Gita Gopi and LS Pirzada declined the plea after considering a medical report stating that Asaram's wife had responded well to treatment and was expected to be discharged within 2-3 days. “When the patient has responded well to the treatment and both the doctors have opined that she would be discharged within the next two to three days, we do not find any reason to allow the application of the petitioner, who is presently in Jodhpur Jail, Rajasthan,” said the Court. However, the Court allowed Asaram to seek permission from the jail authorities to communicate with his wife through video conferencing. [EY Vs Union of India] The appeal challenges a June 18 judgment by a Division Bench of Justices V Kameswar Rao and Vinod Kumar , which ruled in favour of the Income Tax Department on the secondment issue. The judgment arose from five appeals concerning assessment years 2018-19 to 2022-23. The Income Tax Appellate Tribunal (ITAT) earlier ruled in favour of EY US and treated the payments as cost-to-cost reimbursements. It also held that the seconded personnel became employees of the Indian entities during the period of their secondment. The High Court disagreed with the ITAT. items.title: How can we make International Arbitration truly successful in India?
items.summary: Recently, I had the opportunity to interact with a very seasoned and experienced Senior Counsel from Singapore. Our conversation moved towards a subject that has been discussed extensively in India over the last few years: can India become a global hub for international arbitration? His answer surprised me. He said, quite simply, that India can never become an international arbitration hub. At first, I thought this was criticism. It wasn't. His reasoning was far more interesting. According to him, India is too large an economy, too significant a market and too important a participant in global commerce to merely aspire to become an "arbitration hub" in the conventional sense of the term. Countries such as Singapore, London, Paris or Hong Kong have developed themselves as preferred seats for international arbitration for a variety of historical, commercial, institutional and legal reasons. India, however, has an opportunity to build something much larger. India does not necessarily need to become an international arbitration hub. items.title: EAM Jaishankar warns of food crisis, Opposition targets Modi govt on readiness
items.summary: External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar has warned that a major global food crisis could hit in the coming months, driven by severe fertiliser shortages, blocked grain shipments, and ongoing wars. Speaking at an Asia Society event in New York, Jaishankar said expanding conflicts in eastern Europe and West Asia are squeezing trade routes and hitting developing nations the hardest. Jaishankar pointed out that key grain exporters are struggling to ship supplies through the Black Sea, while major fertiliser producers in Russia and West Asia face heavy production and transit disruptions. Combined with tight energy markets, capital flight, and extreme weather patterns like El Niño, he said the global economy is facing a combined squeeze on food, fuel, fertiliser, and finance. He also criticised richer nations for taking self-centred policy decisions that ignore the basic needs of vulnerable countries. The Minister’s statements quickly triggered sharp reactions from domestic opposition parties, who accused the Union government of using global problems to cover up internal mismanagement. Senior Advocate Arvind Datar , appearing for Daiichi, said the company had pursued arbitration, obtained an award on April 29, 2016 and then initiated execution proceedings, but was yet to realise the award. " It’s 10 years to execute an award, international award ,” Datar said.
